contentChunks.htmlValue: Usage

Dividers are one way to visually group components and create hierarchy. They can also be used to imply nested parent/child relationships.

The divider can be used in two ways: 

  1. Full width

  2. Inset

contentChunks.altText: Inbox app using full-width dividers to separate messages.
Music app using inset dividers to separate songs in a playlist.

contentChunks.htmlValue: Anatomy
A divider is a simple line.
Full-width dividers

Use full-width dividers to separate larger sections of unrelated content. They can be used directly on a surface or inside other components like cards or lists.

Full-width dividers can also separate interactive areas from non-interactive areas. 

They are used to group visual elements together, and indicate when elements are related to each other from an interaction perspective.

contentChunks.footer: Full-width dividers to indicate separation of content
contentChunks.altText: Inbox messages visually separated by full-width dividers for improved readability.

contentChunks.footer: Use full-width divider lines to separate interactive and non-interactive areas of a container such as a card
contentChunks.altText: Non-interactive information on a card and a clickable read more link separated by a full-width divider.

contentChunks.footer: Use full-width dividers sparingly. Too many divider lines will make an interface look cluttered.
contentChunks.altText: Full-width dividers used after every piece of content on a page.

contentChunks.htmlValue: Inset dividers

Use inset dividers to separate related content within a section.

Inset dividers are equally indented from both sides of the screen by default.

contentChunks.footer: Inset dividers separate related content, such as emails in a list. They should be used with anchoring elements such as icons or avatars, and align with the leading edge of the screen.
contentChunks.altText: 2 different content sections separated by an inset divider.

contentChunks.footer: Inset dividers in a list of related items
contentChunks.altText: 3 types of related content separated by inset dividers on a mobile screen.

contentChunks.footer: Inset dividers can be placed in the middle of a layout to separate elements such as body text from selection chips
contentChunks.altText: Inset divider separating body text and selection chips.

contentChunks.htmlValue:
Using dividers both ways on the same screen

If dividers are used both ways in a UI, they must reinforce the hierarchy of information within different sections.

  1. To separate a different kind of content, use a full-width divider

  2. To separate nested content items, use inset dividers

contentChunks.footer: Use a combination of inset and full-width dividers to reflect the hierarchy of information
contentChunks.altText: Dividers used to show content hierarchy: full-width for sections, inset for related items.

contentChunks.htmlValue: List items with repetitive formats may not require an inset divider, in which using only the margin between items is acceptable.

contentChunks.footer: Content may not require a divider line
contentChunks.altText: List with repetitive item formats. Visual separation achieved through margins only.

contentChunks.htmlValue: Vertical divider
A vertical divider can be used to arrange content on a larger screen, such as separating paragraph text from video or imagery media.

contentChunks.footer: Vertical divider in a large screen context
contentChunks.altText: Image and text side-by-side, separated by a vertical divider on a large screen.

contentChunks.htmlValue: Dividers are decorative elements, which have no contrast minimums.

contentChunks.footer: Decorative elements have no contrast minimums
